2:44.sourceText: νομίσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ συνοδίᾳ ἦλθον ἡμέρας ὁδὸν καὶ ἀνεζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γνωστοῖς,
2:44.targetText: and having supposed Him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey, and were seeking Him among the relatives and among the acquaintances,

groups.note: The actual ἐν governs both coordinated relatives and acquaintances. English repeats among with the second group; both repetitions retain this one genuinely shared source preposition.

2:45.sourceText: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἀναζητοῦντες αὐτόν.
2:45.targetText: and having not found Him, they turned back to Jerusalem seeking Him.

groups.note: The actual Him object of seeking is also the same immediately preceding not-found search object. English states that same searched-for person twice, found Him and seeking Him, without a separately written second pronoun.

2:46.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς εὗρον αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καθεζόμενον ἐν μέσῳ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀκούοντα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶντα αὐτούς·
2:46.targetText: And it came to pass, after three days they found Him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both hearing them and questioning them,

2:47.sourceText: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ συνέσει καὶ ταῖς ἀποκρίσεσιν αὐτοῦ.
2:47.targetText: and all those hearing Him were astonished at His understanding and answers.

2:48.sourceText: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεπλάγησαν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ Τέκνον, τί ἐποίησας ἡμῖν οὕτως; ἰδοὺ ὁ πατήρ σου κἀγὼ ὀδυνώμενοι ζητοῦμέν σε.
2:48.targetText: And having seen Him, they were amazed, and His mother said to Him, “Child, why did You do this to us? Behold, Your father and I, sorrowing, were seeking You.”

groups.note: The actual manner adverb οὕτως, thus/in this way, qualifies what was done. English recasts that same deed/manner as the object this; no source τοῦτο demonstrative is invented.
N1904 writes the present we seek, ζητοῦμεν; LSV narrates past were seeking. The same actual searching head and people are retained with that tense wording difference explicit.

2:49.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με; οὐκ ᾔδειτε ὅτι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Πατρός μου δεῖ εἶναί με;
2:49.targetText: And He said to them, “Why [is it] that you were seeking Me? Did you not know that it is necessary for Me to be in the things of My Father?”

groups.note: The actual being infinitive with its accusative Me subject supplies the necessary-action content, rendered for Me to be. The complete infinitival clause supplies the English subject-introducing for, not a written Greek for preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an explicit copular question frame in why is it that; the Greek has τί ὅτι without a written be verb there.

2:52.sourceText: Καὶ Ἰησοῦς προέκοπτεν ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ Θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις.
2:52.targetText: and Jesus was advancing in wisdom, and in stature, and in favor with God and men.

groups.note: The one actual ἐν governs all three coordinated growth domains. English repeats in before stature and favor; all three English prepositions retain the same genuinely shared source relation.
The actual ἡλικία can denote age or stature; LSV chooses stature here. The original head stays visible rather than substituting a different Greek bodily-size noun.
